text_blocks.snippet: COVID-19 pneumonia is a lung infection caused by the SARS-CoV-2 virus, which can lead to inflammation and fluid buildup in the lungs. It can range in severity from mild to severe, and anyone can develop it, though older individuals and those with other health conditions are at higher risk, according to the Cleveland Clinic and WebMD. Symptoms can include cough, fever, shortness of breath, and fatigue.
snippet_highlighted_words: a lung infection caused by the SARS-CoV-2 virus, which can lead to inflammation and fluid buildup in the lungs

list.title: Severity:
list.snippet: COVID-19 pneumonia can range from mild to severe, potentially requiring hospitalization and even ventilation.

list.title: Risk Factors:
list.snippet: Older adults, especially those 65 and older, are at increased risk, with those 85 and older being at the highest risk according to WebMD. People with underlying health conditions are also more susceptible according to the Cleveland Clinic.

list.title: Symptoms:
list.snippet: Common symptoms include cough, fever, shortness of breath, and fatigue.

list.title: Prevention:
list.snippet: Vaccination against COVID-19 and pneumococcal disease, practicing good hygiene (handwashing), avoiding close contact with infected individuals, and managing underlying health conditions are important preventive measures according to the Cleveland Clinic.

list.title: Treatment:
list.snippet: Treatment may involve oxygen therapy, antiviral medications, and other supportive care depending on the severity of the pneumonia.
